title: 4 ways to tell a great story

lines.en: Your first job as a speaker is to build a trusting human bond with your audience.
lines.zh: 身為講者，你的第一份工作是和觀眾建立信任的人際連結。

lines.en: One excellent way to connect to an audience is to tell a story.
lines.zh: 和觀眾建立連結的絕佳方法之一，就是說故事。

lines.en: Stories helped make us who we are.
lines.zh: 故事幫助塑造了今天的我們。

lines.en: Really — evidence left behind from our ancient ancestors suggests that the human mind developed alongside human storytelling.
lines.zh: 真的，遠古祖先留下的證據顯示，人類心智是隨著說故事一起發展的。

lines.en: Fire created a new magnet for bonding.
lines.zh: 火成了一個新的凝聚磁鐵。

lines.en: Its warmth and flickering light drew people together after dark.
lines.zh: 它的溫暖和搖曳的光，在天黑後把人們聚在一起。

lines.en: This seems to have happened in every ancient culture over the last 300,000 years.
lines.zh: 這似乎在過去 30 萬年來的每個古文化中都發生過。

lines.en: And what did our ancestors do with this time together?
lines.zh: 那我們的祖先在一起的時候都做些什麼？

lines.en: In many cultures, one type of communal activity became very important: storytelling.
lines.zh: 在許多文化中，有一種群體活動變得非常重要：說故事。

lines.en: Stories brought people from faraway places to the fireside.
lines.zh: 故事把遠方的人們帶到火堆旁。

lines.en: Stories about people who were alive and people who were dead, nearby and in distant lands.
lines.zh: 關於活著的人和死去的人的故事，關於附近和遙遠國度的故事。

lines.en: Stories sparked laughter, tension, and amazement.
lines.zh: 故事引發歡笑、緊張和驚奇。

lines.en: Stories also played an important role in helping expand people’s ability to imagine and to dream, and to understand the minds of others.
lines.zh: 故事也在幫助人們擴展想像與夢想的能力、理解他人想法上扮演重要角色。

lines.en: Storytellers became important people within a community, and their listeners took information from the stories that changed how they behaved in the world.
lines.zh: 說故事的人成了社群中的重要人物，聽眾從故事中獲取資訊，改變他們在世上的行為方式。

lines.en: It's not just that we all love hearing stories.
lines.zh: 不只是我們都愛聽故事而已。

lines.en: Stories probably helped shape how our minds share and receive information.
lines.zh: 故事很可能幫助塑造了我們的大腦分享與接收資訊的方式。

lines.en: So it's no surprise that many of the best talks are built around a story.
lines.zh: 所以很多最棒的演講都是圍繞一個故事建構的，這並不意外。

lines.en: The most basic way of breaking down a story is this: a character with a goal meets an unexpected obstacle.
lines.zh: 拆解故事最基本的方式是：一個有目標的角色遇到意想不到的阻礙。

lines.en: She tries to overcome that obstacle, which builds to a peak in the action.
lines.zh: 她試圖克服那個阻礙，情節因此推向高潮。

lines.en: Finally, there’s some kind of resolution to the conflict.
lines.zh: 最後，衝突以某種方式得到解決。

lines.en: When it comes to sharing a story from the stage, remember four key things.
lines.zh: 在台上分享故事時，記住四個關鍵。

lines.en: 1. Base the story around a character your audience can empathize with.
lines.zh: 一，以觀眾能產生共鳴的角色為故事核心。

lines.en: 2. Build tension, either through curiosity, relationship with other characters, or actual danger.
lines.zh: 二，營造緊張感，可以透過好奇心、和其他角色的關係，或是真正的危險。

lines.en: 3. Offer the right level of detail.
lines.zh: 三，提供適量的細節。

lines.en: If there's not enough, the story won't come to life.
lines.zh: 如果細節不夠，故事就不會生動。

lines.en: If there's too much, it will get bogged down.
lines.zh: 如果細節太多，故事就會拖沓。

lines.en: And, 4. End with a satisfying conclusion, whether it’s funny, moving, or surprising.
lines.zh: 還有，四，用令人滿意的結尾收尾，不論是好笑、感人還是出人意料。

lines.en: Some great talks are built around a single story.
lines.zh: 有些很棒的演講就只圍繞一個故事。

lines.en: This can be really helpful for a speaker.
lines.zh: 這對講者來說很有幫助。

lines.en: The throughline is simply the plot of the story.
lines.zh: 主軸就是故事的情節本身。

lines.en: If the story is about you, it can even create empathy in the audience.
lines.zh: 如果故事是關於你自己，甚至能讓觀眾產生同理心。

lines.en: If your journey is exciting and easy to follow, this type of talk can work really well.
lines.zh: 如果你的經歷精彩又容易理解，這種演講效果會很好。

lines.en: But there's a trap here too.
lines.zh: 但這裡也有一個陷阱。

lines.en: Remember, the goal is to give.
lines.zh: 記住，目標是給予。

lines.en: Personal stories may entertain or interest an audience, or make the speaker feel really good about themselves,
lines.zh: 個人故事也許能娛樂觀眾、引起興趣，或讓講者自我感覺良好，

lines.en: but they don’t necessarily give the audience something they can walk away with; a new way of understanding things, actionable information, context, hope.
lines.zh: 但不一定能讓觀眾帶走什麼：一種理解事物的新方式、可以付諸行動的資訊、背景脈絡、希望。

lines.en: And that’s a real shame.
lines.zh: 那就真的很可惜了。

lines.en: The key is to link together the important moments of your story in a way that can be meaningful to someone else.
lines.zh: 關鍵是把你故事中的重要時刻，用對別人有意義的方式串連起來。

lines.en: Otherwise, it may sound like you're just rambling or speaking for the sake of hearing yourself talk.
lines.zh: 否則聽起來可能像是在漫無目的地閒扯，或只是為了聽自己說話而說。

lines.en: But, if the journey reveals something powerful you have learned, and if each step in your journey is revealed with humility and honesty and vulnerability, it is a journey we will gladly take with you.
lines.zh: 但如果這段旅程揭示了你學到的深刻道理，而且每一步都以謙遜、誠實和坦露脆弱的方式呈現，那我們會很樂意和你一起走這段旅程。

lines.en: There is one other piece that is absolutely essential if you’re going to tell your own story: it has to be true.
lines.zh: 如果你要講自己的故事，還有一件絕對必要的事：它必須是真的。

lines.en: This may seem obvious, but sometimes speakers are tempted to exaggerate or even make a story up entirely.
lines.zh: 這看起來很理所當然，但有時講者會忍不住誇大，甚至完全捏造故事。

lines.en: Stories can have such a big impact that some speakers are tempted to bend the truth.
lines.zh: 故事的影響力可以非常大，以至於有些講者忍不住扭曲事實。

lines.en: But even small exaggerations can quickly destroy your reputation.
lines.zh: 但即使是小小的誇大，也可能迅速毀掉你的名聲。

lines.en: It's not worth the risk.
lines.zh: 這不值得冒險。

lines.en: When you combine a truthful story with a desire to benefit others, you can give your listeners an extraordinary gift.
lines.zh: 當你把真實的故事和造福他人的心意結合起來，就能給聽眾一份非凡的禮物。

lines.en: A story can affect people deeply.
lines.zh: 一個故事可以深深打動人心。

lines.en: Use it, and you can greatly increase your connection with an audience.
lines.zh: 善用它，你就能大大增加和觀眾之間的連結。

lines.en: But please, let it mean something.
lines.zh: 但請讓它有意義。
